[engine] A build fingerprint must be discovered by glob over every shared library the run loads (`libggml*.dylib`, `libllama*.dylib`, the server binary), never from a hand-picked file list; a knob whose code lives in a library the fingerprint does not hash makes two genuinely different builds compare as one.

<!-- lesson_id: eng-mh-0007 | class: measurement-hygiene | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `measurement-hygiene`

## 為什麼（because）

Today's gate fix lives in ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp, which links into libggml-base.0.19.0.dylib (proved by build/ggml/src/CMakeFiles/ggml-base.dir/ggml-backend.cpp.o, not by inference). decode_sweep.py:33 and ab_interleave.py:42 hash exactly three files -- llama-server, libggml-metal.0.19.0.dylib, libllama.0.0.239.dylib -- so the pair taken at 21:34 (gate NOT yet fixed: both noasync arms bit-copied their segmented counterparts) and the pair taken at 21:41 (gate fixed: p25-slotgpu-noasync = {ff68c5a2}) carry the SAME fingerprint server=131bc5316ebf metal=9729ad35ddd1 llama=9066e1697a58. The project's own rule is 'compare only within one fingerprint', so the two runs were stamped comparable while their scheduler code differed. Secondary defect in the same function: the paths contain literal version numbers, so a version bump silently degrades the entry to the string "missing" instead of failing.
